critical.issue: FIXED BY TESTING AGENT: send_monthly_report used tuple((..., await usage_xlsx(...)) for dv in devs) - a generator expression containing await becomes an async generator -> TypeError 'async_generator' object is not iterable -> HTTP 500 whenever the client had at least one admin. The scheduled 1st-of-month job would also have silently failed (caught and logged). Changed to tuple([...]) list comprehension (server.py line ~1426).

minor.issue: monthly_tick() is called inside the same try as reset_manual_to_auto(); if reset_manual_to_auto raises at 06:00 on the 1st, the monthly report is skipped for that month (only runs when strftime=='06:00'). Consider separate try blocks, and/or a catch-up check (e.g. day==1 and hour>=6 and no monthly_reports key) so a backend restart/sleep at 06:00 does not lose the report.
Forced send writes the dedupe key for the previous month even when status is not_configured/failed; harmless for the previous month but means a failed SMTP send is never retried automatically.

ui_bugs.issue: Download button label is always 'Pobierz CSV' (i18n key download) even when Excel format is selected (default). Should be neutral 'Pobierz' or switch to 'Pobierz Excel'/'Pobierz CSV' per fmt; card title key is also named exportCsv.

issues: Active cycle per-head % compares a partial (in-progress) cycle against full previous cycles, so it will almost always show large green negative % early in the cycle (e.g. day 5 shows -80%). Consider normalising per day (l/head/day) or labelling it as 'do tej pory' to avoid misleading comparison.

rca of the issue: POST /monthly-report/send 500: `tuple((name, await f(x)) for x in xs)` inside async def -> Python compiles a generator expression containing await as an async generator; tuple() cannot iterate it -> TypeError. Reproduce: create admin user for client, POST /api/monthly-report/send?client_id=... -> 500 (backend.err.log line server.py:1426). Mitigation: list comprehension tuple([...]) (applied) - retested 200 with status ['not_configured'].
